title: حكاية ملك شهريار واخيه
titleEn: The Tale of King Shahriyār and His Brother
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 1–3, transcribed by eye from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn); the edition’s OCR is unusable. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition’s — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved unaltered. Audio follows one stated convention: a Modern Standard Arabic reading of the classical text — an admitted choice, since no one knows how a Cairo storyteller sounded.
about: Every printed edition of the Nights, this one included, belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights by absorbing whatever was to hand. No printed edition is a medieval text; the medieval witness is the Syrian branch, and a second edition of this same passage from the fourteenth-century Galland manuscript is planned. Macnaghten also regularized the language toward Classical Arabic here and there, so some of the original Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit. Where the text’s own grammar is non-Classical it has been vocalized as it stands and flagged in the notes, not quietly repaired. The tale is frank about sex and violence and is translated that way.

sentences.t: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ وَالصَّلَوةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى سَيِّدِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ سَيِّدِنَا وَمَوْلَانَا مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ صَلَوةً وَسَلَامًا دَائِمَيْنِ مُتَلَازِمَيْنِ إِلَى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ
sentences.tr: al-ḥamdu li-llāhi rabbi al-ʿālamīna wa-al-ṣalātu wa-al-salāmu ʿalā sayyidi al-mursalīna sayyidinā wa-mawlānā Muḥammadin ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama ṣalātan wa-salāman dāʾimayni mutalāzimayni ilā yawmi al-dīn
sentences.l: The praise (belongs) to God, Lord of the worlds, and the blessing and the peace (be) upon the lord of the sent-ones, our lord and our master Muḥammad — God blessed him and granted-him-peace — a blessing and a peace, both-lasting, both-inseparable, until the Day of the Judgment.
sentences.i: Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds; and blessing and peace be upon the chief of the Messengers, our lord and master Muhammad — may God bless him and grant him peace — a blessing and a peace enduring and unceasing, until the Day of Judgment.
sentences.n: The whole doxology is sajʿ (rhymed prose): al-ʿālamīn / al-mursalīn / dāʾimayn / mutalāzimayn / al-dīn all close on -īn or -ayn. صلوة is the older orthography with wāw, kept exactly as the edition prints it; it is read ṣalāh. The duals دَائِمَيْنِ مُتَلَازِمَيْنِ agree with the pair "a blessing and a peace."

sentences.t: وَبَعْدُ فَإِنَّ سِيَرَ الْأَوَّلِينَ صَارَتْ عِبْرَةً لِلْآخِرِينَ لِيَرَى الْإِنْسَانُ الْعِبَرَ الَّتِي حَصَلَتْ لِغَيْرِهِ فَيَعْتَبِرَ وَيُطَالِعَ حَدِيثَ الْأُمَمِ السَّالِفَةِ وَمَا جَرَى لَهُمْ فَيَنْزَجِرَ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿdu fa-inna siyara al-awwalīna ṣārat ʿibratan li-al-ākhirīna li-yarā al-insānu al-ʿibara allatī ḥaṣalat li-ghayrihi fa-yaʿtabira wa-yuṭāliʿa ḥadītha al-umami al-sālifati wa-mā jarā lahum fa-yanzajir
sentences.l: And after (that): indeed the life-stories of the former-ones became an admonition for the later-ones, so that the human-being may see the lessons that befell someone-other-than-himself and so take-warning, and may peruse the account of the bygone nations and what befell them, and so be-restrained.
sentences.i: To proceed: the histories of former peoples have become an admonition to those who come after, that a man may look upon the reverses which befell others and take warning thereby, and may study the chronicles of the nations gone by and what befell them, and so be held back.
sentences.n: وَبَعْدُ is the transition formula (short for أَمَّا بَعْدُ) that turns from the doxology to the business at hand; بَعْدُ is indeclinable in -u because its complement is left unspoken. The purpose-lām of لِيَرَى governs the whole chain in the subjunctive: يَرَى … فَيَعْتَبِرَ … وَيُطَالِعَ … فَيَنْزَجِرَ. The sajʿ falls on فَيَعْتَبِرَ / فَيَنْزَجِرَ, and earlier on الْأَوَّلِينَ / الْآخِرِينَ.

sentences.t: فَسُبْحَانَ مَنْ جَعَلَ حَدِيثَ الْأَوَّلِينَ عِبْرَةً لِقَوْمِ الْآخِرِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-subḥāna man jaʿala ḥadītha al-awwalīna ʿibratan li-qawmi al-ākhirīn
sentences.l: So glory-be-to Him who made the account of the former-ones an admonition for the folk of the later-ones.
sentences.i: Glory, then, to Him who made the tale of the ancients an admonition to the folk of later days.
sentences.n: سُبْحَانَ is a frozen accusative (the cognate object of an unexpressed verb) and appears only in this glorifying formula — followed either by a genitive, as here, or by a pronoun suffix (سُبْحَانَكَ 'glory be to You'). مَنْ here is the relative pronoun 'he who', not the interrogative 'who?'.

sentences.t: فَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْعِبَرُ الْحِكَايَاتُ الَّتِي تُسَمَّى أَلْفَ لَيْلَةٍ وَلَيْلَةً وَمَا فِيهَا مِنَ السِّيَرِ الْجَلِيلَةِ وَالْأَمْثَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-min dhālika al-ʿibaru al-ḥikāyātu allatī tusammā alfa laylatin wa-laylatan wa-mā fīhā mina al-siyari al-jalīlati wa-al-amthāl
sentences.l: And of that (sort) are the admonitions — the tales which are called A Thousand Nights and a Night — and what is in them of the noble life-stories and the parables.
sentences.i: An instance of this is those admonitions, the tales that are called the Thousand and One Nights, and the noble histories and parables contained therein.
sentences.n: فَمِنْ ذَلِكَ is the standard 'an instance of this is…'; الْعِبَرُ is then the nominative subject and الْحِكَايَاتُ stands in apposition to it. One may instead read الْعِبَرِ in the genitive ('among those admonitions'), but ذَلِكَ (m. sg.) would then disagree with the f. pl. — possible in Middle Arabic. أَلْف takes a singular genitive (لَيْلَةٍ), and وَلَيْلَةً is coordinated with the accusative أَلْفَ.

sentences.t: فَقَدْ حُكِيَ ( وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِغَيْبِهِ وَأَحْكَمُ وَأَعَزُّ وَأَكْرَمُ وَأَلْطَفُ وَأَرْحَمُ ) فِيمَا مَضَى وَتَقَدَّمَ وَنُسْلِفُ مِنْ أَحَادِيثِ الْأُمَمِ
sentences.tr: fa-qad ḥukiya ( wa-Allāhu aʿlamu bi-ghaybihi wa-aḥkamu wa-aʿazzu wa-akramu wa-alṭafu wa-arḥamu ) fīmā maḍā wa-taqaddama wa-nuslifu min aḥādīthi al-umam
sentences.l: And indeed it has-been-related — and God is more-knowing of His hidden, and wiser, and mightier, and more-generous, and more-gracious, and more-merciful — concerning what has passed and gone-before and (what) we set-down-in-advance, of the accounts of the nations.
sentences.i: Now it has been told — and God is the better knower of what He keeps hidden, and the wiser, the mightier, the more bountiful, the more gracious, the more merciful — touching that which is past and long gone by, and that which we here set down, out of the chronicles of the nations.
sentences.n: The parenthesis is a chain of elatives (أَفْعَل forms), a pious hedge slipped in before the storytelling starts; the round brackets are the editor's, and the rhyme runs aḥkam / akram / arḥam / al-umam. وَنُسْلِفُ is anomalous — a first-person plural imperfect ('and we set forth in advance') where the parallel with مَضَى وَتَقَدَّمَ would lead one to expect a perfect; it is vocalized here as printed rather than repaired.

sentences.t: أَنَّهُ كَانَ فِي قَدِيمِ الزَّمَانِ وَسَالِفِ الْعَصْرِ وَالْأَوَانِ مَلِكٌ مِنْ مُلُوكِ بَنِي سَاسَانَ بِجَزَائِرِ الْهِنْدِ وَالصِّينِ صَاحِبُ جُنْدٍ وَأَعْوَانٍ وَخَدَمٍ وَحَشَمٍ
sentences.tr: annahu kāna fī qadīmi al-zamāni wa-sālifi al-ʿaṣri wa-al-awāni malikun min mulūki banī Sāsāna bi-jazāʾiri al-Hindi wa-al-Ṣīni ṣāḥibu jundin wa-aʿwānin wa-khadamin wa-ḥasham
sentences.l: — that there was, in the old of time and the bygone of the age and the season, a king among the kings of the sons of Sāsān, in the islands of India and China, possessor of troops and auxiliaries and servants and retinue.
sentences.i: — that in olden time and in ages long past there was a king among the kings of the House of Sasan, in the isles of India and China, master of armies and auxiliaries, of servants and household.
sentences.n: This clause hangs on حُكِيَ in the preceding unit: 'it has been told … that there was.' The sajʿ is on -ān: الزَّمَان / الْأَوَان / سَاسَان / أَعْوَان, then a second pair خَدَم / حَشَم. بِـ in بِجَزَائِرِ is locative, an ordinary alternative to فِي.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ لَهُ وَلَدَانِ أَحَدُهُمَا كَبِيرٌ وَالْآخَرُ صَغِيرٌ وَكَانَا فَارِسَيْنِ بَطَلَيْنِ وَكَانَ الْأَكْبَرُ أَفْرَسَ مِنَ الْأَصْغَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna lahu waladāni aḥaduhumā kabīrun wa-al-ākharu ṣaghīrun wa-kānā fārisayni baṭalayni wa-kāna al-akbaru afrasa mina al-aṣghar
sentences.l: And there were to him two sons, one-of-the-two elder and the other younger, and the two were two-horsemen, two-champions; and the elder was more-horsemanly than the younger.
sentences.i: He had two sons, the one elder and the other younger, and both were horsemen and champions; but the elder was the better horseman of the two.
sentences.n: كَبِير and صَغِير here mean 'elder' and 'younger', not 'large' and 'small'. أَفْرَس is an elative built straight from the noun فَارِس 'horseman' — 'more of a horseman' — a formation the grammarians disapprove of but which is quite at home in this prose.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ مَلَكَ الْبِلَادَ وَحَكَمَ بِالْعَدْلِ فِي الرَّعِيَّةِ وَأَحَبُّوهُ أَهْلُ بِلَادِهِ وَمَمْلَكَتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad malaka al-bilāda wa-ḥakama bi-al-ʿadli fī al-raʿiyyati wa-aḥabbūhu ahlu bilādihi wa-mamlakatih
sentences.l: And he had ruled the lands and judged with justice among the subjects, and they-loved-him, the people of his lands and his kingdom.
sentences.i: He held the lands in his hand and governed his subjects with justice, and the people of his lands and his kingdom loved him.
sentences.n: وَأَحَبُّوهُ أَهْلُ بِلَادِهِ puts the plural ending on the verb even though its subject follows — the construction the grammarians nickname akalūnī l-barāghīth ('the fleas ate me'). Strict Classical usage would give وَأَحَبَّهُ أَهْلُ بِلَادِهِ. It is a regular feature of this narrative Arabic and will recur.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ اسْمُهُ الْمَلِكَ شَهْرِيَارَ وَكَانَ أَخُوهُ الصَّغِيرُ اسْمُهُ الْمَلِكَ شَاهْ زَمَانَ وَكَانَ مَلِكَ سَمَرْقَنْدَ الْعَجَمِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna ismuhu al-Malika Shahriyāra wa-kāna akhūhu al-ṣaghīru ismuhu al-Malika Shāh Zamāna wa-kāna malika Samarqanda al-ʿajam
sentences.l: And his name was King Shahriyar; and his younger brother — his name was King Shahzaman, and he was king of Samarqand of the Persians.
sentences.i: His name was King Shahriyar; and his younger brother was named King Shahzaman, and he was king of Samarqand of the Persians.
sentences.n: The second clause is topic-and-comment: 'his younger brother — his name was …', with كَانَ taking أَخُوهُ as its subject and the whole nominal sentence اسْمُهُ الْمَلِكَ شَاهْ زَمَانَ as its predicate. شَاهْ زَمَان is Persian, 'king of the age'; the first element stays indeclinable and the case falls on زَمَان. الْعَجَم means the non-Arabs, in practice the Persians — 'Samarqand of the Persians'.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَالَا مُسْتَمِرَّيْنِ فِي بِلَادِهِمَا وَكُلُّ وَاحِدٍ فِي مَمْلَكَتِهِ حَاكِمٌ عَادِلٌ فِي رَعِيَّتِهِ مُدَّةَ عِشْرِينَ سَنَةً فِي غَايَةِ الْبَسْطِ وَالِانْشِرَاحِ وَلَمْ يَزَالَا عَلَى هَذِهِ الْحَالَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazālā mustamirrayni fī bilādihimā wa-kullu wāḥidin fī mamlakatihi ḥākimun ʿādilun fī raʿiyyatihi muddata ʿishrīna sanatan fī ghāyati al-basṭi wa-al-inshirāḥi wa-lam yazālā ʿalā hādhihi al-ḥāla
sentences.l: And the two of them did not cease being continuing in their two lands — and each one, in his kingdom, a ruler just toward his flock — for the span of twenty years, in the utmost of ease and gladness; and the two of them did not cease upon this state.
sentences.i: And so the two of them remained settled in their several lands, each in his own kingdom a ruler just toward his subjects, for the space of twenty years, in the fullest contentment and delight; and in this condition they continued.
sentences.n: لَمْ يَزَالَا is the dual of the 'verb of continuance' zāla: literally 'the two did not cease [being]', idiomatically 'they went on being'. Its predicate stands in the accusative — hence the dual accusative مُسْتَمِرَّيْنِ. You will meet this construction constantly in the Nights; from here on it can simply be read as 'they continued'.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ اشْتَاقَ الْمَلِكُ الْكَبِيرُ إِلَى أَخِيهِ الصَّغِيرِ فَأَمَرَ وَزِيرَهُ أَنْ يُسَافِرَ إِلَى عِنْدِ أَخِيهِ وَيُحْضِرَ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika ishtāqa al-maliku al-kabīru ilā akhīhi al-ṣaghīri fa-amara wazīrahu an yusāfira ilā ʿindi akhīhi wa-yuḥḍira bih
sentences.l: So at that, the elder king longed toward his younger brother, and he ordered his vizier that he should travel to at his brother's and bring with him.
sentences.i: Thereupon the elder king was seized with longing for his younger brother, and he commanded his vizier to journey to where his brother was and fetch him.
sentences.n: Two Middle Arabic turns here. إِلَى عِنْدَ stacks two prepositional words — Classical would say إِلَى أَخِيهِ; the edition's 'to at his brother's' is idiomatic later Arabic. And يُحْضِرَ بِهِ 'bring with him' uses bi- to mark the object of an already-transitive verb IV; read it simply as 'bring him'.

sentences.t: فَأَجَابَهُ بِالسَّمْعِ وَالطَّاعَةِ وَسَافَرَ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلَ بِالسَّلَامَةِ وَدَخَلَ إِلَى عِنْدِ أَخِيهِ وَبَلَّغَهُ السَّلَامَ وَأَعْلَمَهُ أَنَّ أَخَاهُ مُشْتَاقٌ إِلَيْهِ وَقَصْدَهُ بِزِيَارَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ajābahu bi-al-samʿi wa-al-ṭāʿati wa-sāfara ilā an waṣala bi-al-salāmati wa-dakhala ilā ʿindi akhīhi wa-ballaghahu al-salāma wa-aʿlamahu anna akhāhu mushtāqun ilayhi wa-qaṣdahu bi-ziyāratih
sentences.l: So he answered him with hearing and obedience, and he travelled until he arrived in safety, and he entered in to at his brother's, and conveyed to him the greeting, and informed him that his brother was longing for him, and [that] his aim was in visiting him.
sentences.i: He answered him with hearing and obedience and journeyed on until he arrived in safety. He came in to the king's brother, delivered the greeting to him, and told him that Shahriyar pined for him and desired a visit of him.
sentences.n: بِالسَّمْعِ وَالطَّاعَةِ — 'with hearing and obedience' — is the fixed formula of a subordinate accepting an order, the Arabic equivalent of 'I hear and I obey.' It is an answer in itself, and recurs verbatim throughout the Nights. Also note إِلَى أَنْ + perfect, 'until such time as', where MSA would more often use ḥattā.

sentences.t: فَأَجَابَهُ بِالسَّمْعِ وَالطَّاعَةِ وَتَجَهَّزَ لِلسَّفَرِ وَأَخْرَجَ خِيَامَهُ وَجِمَالَهُ وَبِغَالَهُ وَخَدَمَهُ وَأَعْوَانَهُ وَأَقَامَ وَزِيرَهُ حَاكِمًا فِي بِلَادِهِ وَخَرَجَ طَالِبًا بِلَادَ أَخِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ajābahu bi-al-samʿi wa-al-ṭāʿati wa-tajahhaza li-al-safari wa-akhraja khiyāmahu wa-jimālahu wa-bighālahu wa-khadamahu wa-aʿwānahu wa-aqāma wazīrahu ḥākiman fī bilādihi wa-kharaja ṭāliban bilāda akhīh
sentences.l: So he answered him with hearing and obedience, and he made himself ready for the journey, and he brought out his tents and his camels and his mules and his servants and his aides, and he set up his vizier as ruler in his lands, and he went out seeking the lands of his brother.
sentences.i: He answered him with hearing and obedience and made ready for the journey. He brought forth his tents, his camels, his mules, his servants and his retainers; he installed his vizier as governor over his lands, and set out for his brother's country.
sentences.n: حَاكِمًا and طَالِبًا are both accusatives of circumstance (ḥāl): 'as a ruler', 'seeking'. Arabic habitually turns what English makes a subordinate clause ('so that he should rule', 'in order to reach') into a single accusative participle.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ فِي نِصْفِ اللَّيْلِ تَذَكَّرَ حَاجَةً نَسِيَهَا فِي قَصْرِهِ فَرَجَعَ وَدَخَلَ قَصْرَهُ فَوَجَدَ زَوْجَتَهُ رَاقِدَةً فِي فِرَاشِهِ مُعَانِقَةً عَبْدًا أَسْوَدَ مِنْ بَعْضِ الْعَبِيدِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna fī niṣfi al-layli tadhakkara ḥājatan nasiyahā fī qaṣrihi fa-rajaʿa wa-dakhala qaṣrahu fa-wajada zawjatahu rāqidatan fī firāshihi muʿāniqatan ʿabdan aswada min baʿḍi al-ʿabīd
sentences.l: And when it was at the middle of the night, he remembered a thing he needed that he had forgotten in his palace, so he turned back and entered his palace, and he found his wife lying in his bed, embracing a black slave from among the slaves.
sentences.i: When it was midnight, he called to mind something he wanted that he had left behind in his palace; so he turned back and went into his palace, and there he found his wife lying in his bed with her arms about a black slave, one of the slaves.
sentences.n: فَلَمَّا 'and when, as soon as' is the standard narrative hinge of this prose: a lammā-clause with a perfect verb, answered by another perfect. You will see it open nearly every turn of the action from here on. رَاقِدَةً and مُعَانِقَةً are accusative participles of circumstance describing the wife as he found her.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى هَذَا الْأَمْرَ اسْوَدَّتِ الدُّنْيَا فِي وَجْهِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā hādhā al-amra iswaddati al-dunyā fī wajhih
sentences.l: And when he saw this thing, the world turned black in his face.
sentences.i: And when he beheld it, the world turned black before his eyes.
sentences.n: اسْوَدَّتِ الدُّنْيَا فِي وَجْهِهِ is a set idiom of despair and rage — 'the world blackened in his face' — not a description of fainting or of literal darkness. English 'everything went black before his eyes' is close, though the Arabic locates the blackness in the world rather than in the man.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ إِذَا كَانَ هَذَا الْأَمْرُ قَدْ وَقَعَ وَأَنَا مَا فَارَقْتُ الْمَدِينَةَ فَكَيْفَ حَالُ هَذِهِ الْمَلْعُونَةِ لَمَّا أَغِيبُ عِنْدَ أَخِي مُدَّةً
sentences.tr: wa-qāla fī nafsihi idhā kāna hādhā al-amru qad waqaʿa wa-anā mā fāraqtu al-madīnata fa-kayfa ḥālu hādhihi al-malʿūnati lammā aghību ʿinda akhī mudda
sentences.l: And he said within himself: if this matter has already fallen out while I — I have not [even] left the city — then how [will be] the state of this accursed woman when I am absent at my brother's for a period?
sentences.i: And he said within himself: If this has come to pass while I have not so much as quitted the city, what then will become of this accursed woman when I am away at my brother's for a season?
sentences.n: Two departures from the Classical norm. مَا فَارَقْتُ negates the perfect with mā, where Classical prose prefers lam + jussive — a colloquial-leaning usage typical of the Nights' Middle Arabic. And لَمَّا أَغِيبُ uses lammā with the imperfect for future time ('when I shall be away'); in Classical grammar lammā takes the perfect and looks backward, as it does in units 14 and 15.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ سَحَبَ سَيْفَهُ وَضَرَبَ الِاثْنَيْنِ وَقَتَلَهُمَا فِي الْفِرَاشِ وَرَجَعَ مِنْ وَقْتِهِ وَسَاعَتِهِ وَأَمَرَ بِالرَّحِيلِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu saḥaba sayfahu wa-ḍaraba al-ithnayni wa-qatalahumā fī al-firāshi wa-rajaʿa min waqtihi wa-sāʿatihi wa-amara bi-al-raḥīl
sentences.l: Then he drew his sword and struck the two of them and killed them both in the bed, and he returned from his moment and his hour, and gave orders for the departure.
sentences.i: Then he drew his sword and struck the pair of them and slew them both there in the bed; and he turned back that very hour and gave the order to march.
sentences.n: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ 'then indeed he' is a narrative connective of this prose rather than real emphasis — read it as no more than 'then'. مِنْ وَقْتِهِ وَسَاعَتِهِ, 'from his time and his hour', is a fixed doublet meaning 'that very instant, without a moment's delay'.

sentences.t: وَسَارَ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلَ إِلَى مَدِينَةِ أَخِيهِ فَلَمَّا قَرُبَ مَدِينَتَهُ أَرْسَلَ الْمُبَشِّرِينَ إِلَى أَخِيهِ بِقُدُومِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-sāra ilā an waṣala ilā madīnati akhīhi fa-lammā qaruba madīnatahu arsala al-mubashshirīna ilā akhīhi bi-qudūmih
sentences.l: And he journeyed on until he arrived at the city of his brother; and when he drew near his city, he sent the bearers-of-good-tidings to his brother with (news of) his arrival.
sentences.i: And he travelled on until he came to his brother's city; and when he was hard upon it, he sent heralds ahead to his brother to announce his coming.
sentences.n: قَرُبَ normally governs its goal with مِنْ; here the edition has it take a bare accusative object, مَدِينَتَهُ — one of the many places where this text's syntax is Middle Arabic rather than Classical. إِلَى أَنْ + perfect ('until that he arrived') is the ordinary narrative way of saying 'until'.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ إِلَيْهِ وَلَاقَاهُ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ وَفَرِحَ بِهِ غَايَةَ الْفَرَحِ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُ الْمَدِينَةَ وَجَلَسَ مَعَهُ يَتَحَدَّثُ وَيَنْشَرِحُ
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja ilayhi wa-lāqāhu wa-sallama ʿalayhi wa-fariḥa bihi ghāyata al-faraḥi wa-zayyana lahu al-madīnata wa-jalasa maʿahu yataḥaddathu wa-yansharih
sentences.l: So he went out to him, and met him, and greeted him, and rejoiced in him the utmost of rejoicing, and adorned the city for him, and sat with him conversing and taking delight.
sentences.i: So he went forth to meet him and greeted him and rejoiced in him beyond all measure; and he had the city decked out in his honour, and sat with him in talk and good cheer.
sentences.n: غَايَةَ الْفَرَحِ is an adverbial accusative built on the verb's own verbal noun ('rejoiced the utmost of rejoicing') — the standard way this prose piles on intensity; you will meet it constantly. The two imperfects at the end, يَتَحَدَّثُ وَيَنْشَرِحُ, are circumstantial: they describe how he sat, not a further action.

sentences.t: فَتَذَكَّرَ الْمَلِكُ شَاهْ زَمَانُ مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ زَوْجَتِهِ فَحَصَلَ عِنْدَهُ غَمٌّ زَايِدٌ وَاصْفَرَّ لَوْنُهُ وَضَعُفَ جِسْمُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-tadhakkara al-maliku Shāh Zamānu mā kāna min amri zawjatihi fa-ḥaṣala ʿindahu ghammun zāyidun wa-iṣfarra lawnuhu wa-ḍaʿufa jismuh
sentences.l: Then King Shahzaman remembered what had been of the affair of his wife, and there came to be with him an increasing grief, and his colour yellowed, and his body weakened.
sentences.i: Then King Shahzaman called to mind what had passed in the matter of his wife, and a grief that only grew took hold of him: his colour went sallow and his body wasted.
sentences.n: زَايِد is the edition's spelling of Classical زَائِد: in Middle Arabic orthography a medial hamza after ā is regularly written as a bare yāʾ with no hamza seat. اِصْفَرَّ is form IX, the pattern reserved for colours and bodily defects — 'to turn yellow' as a process, not a state. شَاهْ زَمَان is a diptote: the Persian first element stays indeclinable and the case falls on زَمَان, here nominative زَمَانُ as the subject of فَتَذَكَّرَ, without tanwīn.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهُ أَخُوهُ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْحَالَةِ ظَنَّ فِي نَفْسِهِ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ بِسَبَبِ مُفَارَقَتِهِ بِلَادَهُ وَمُلْكَهُ فَتَرَكَ سَبِيلَهُ وَلَمْ يَسْأَلْ عَنْ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhu akhūhu ʿalā hādhihi al-ḥālati ẓanna fī nafsihi anna dhālika bi-sababi mufāraqatihi bilādahu wa-mulkahu fa-taraka sabīlahu wa-lam yasʾal ʿan dhālik
sentences.l: And when his brother saw him in this state, he supposed within himself that that was by reason of his parting-from his lands and his kingdom; so he left his path and did not ask about that.
sentences.i: And when his brother saw him in such a case, he supposed within himself that it came of his having left his country and his kingdom behind; and so he let him be, and asked nothing of the matter.
sentences.n: مُفَارَقَتِهِ بِلَادَهُ is a verbal noun keeping its verb's rection: the suffix ـهِ is its subject ('his parting') and بِلَادَهُ stays accusative as its object — 'his parting-from his lands'. تَرَكَ سَبِيلَهُ, literally 'he left his path', is the idiom for letting someone alone and not pressing him.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ فِي بَعْضِ الْأَيَّامِ قَٰلَ لَهُ يَا أَخِي إِنِّي أَرَاكَ قَدْ ضَعُفَ جِسْمُكَ وَاصْفَرَّ لَوْنُكَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu fī baʿḍi al-ayyāmi qāla lahu yā akhī innī arāka qad ḍaʿufa jismuka wa-iṣfarra lawnuk
sentences.l: Then, on one of the days, he said to him: 'O my brother, I see you — your body has weakened and your colour has yellowed.'
sentences.i: Then upon a certain day he said to him: 'O my brother, I see that your body has grown feeble and your colour sallow.'
sentences.n: The edition prints قل here without the alif of قَالَ (which it spells قال everywhere else) — a common Middle Arabic spelling, not a different word. It is pointed here with a dagger alif (قَٰلَ) so that the printed consonants stand exactly as the edition has them while the word still reads qāla. ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ is a narrative formula, 'then it happened that', where the ـهُ of إِنَّ is a dummy pronoun with no referent. أَرَاكَ قَدْ ضَعُفَ جِسْمُكَ is 'I see you, your body having weakened' — the clause after the object completes the seeing.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا أَخِي أَنَا فِي بَاطِنِي جُرْحٌ وَلَمْ يُخْبِرْهُ بِمَا رَأَى مِنْ زَوْجَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā akhī anā fī bāṭinī jurḥun wa-lam yukhbirhu bimā raʾā min zawjatih
sentences.l: So he said to him: 'O my brother, as for me — within my inward parts is a wound.' And he did not inform him of what he had seen from his wife.
sentences.i: And he answered him: 'O my brother, I carry a wound within me.' But he told him nothing of what he had seen of his wife.
sentences.n: أَنَا فِي بَاطِنِي جُرْحٌ is a topic-comment sentence with no verb: the topic is أَنَا, and the comment is the whole clause فِي بَاطِنِي جُرْحٌ ('in my interior is a wound'). What ties the comment back to the topic is the 1s suffix in بَاطِنِي — the same link the ـه makes in زَيْدٌ أَبُوهُ قَائِمٌ. English has to unpick it as 'I have a wound inside me.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ تُسَافِرَ مَعِي إِلَى الصَّيْدِ وَالْقَنْصِ لَعَلَّ أَنْ يَنْشَرِحَ خَاطِرُكَ فَأَبَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu innī urīdu an tusāfira maʿī ilā al-ṣaydi wa-al-qanṣi laʿalla an yanshariḥa khāṭiruka fa-abā dhālik
sentences.l: So he said to him: 'Indeed I wish that you travel with me to the hunt and the chase; perhaps that your mind may be gladdened.' But he refused that.
sentences.i: Then he said to him: 'It is my wish that you ride out with me to the hunt and the chase, that your spirits may perchance be lifted.' But he would have none of it.
sentences.n: لَعَلَّ 'perhaps' properly takes a noun or pronoun in the accusative; here it is followed by أَنْ + subjunctive, a Middle Arabic construction that treats it like a verb of hoping. الصَّيْد وَالْقَنْص is a paired near-synonym ('hunting and chasing') of the kind this prose loves — English can render it as a doublet or collapse it to one word.

sentences.t: فَسَافَرَ أَخُوةُ وَحْدَةُ إِلَى الصَّيْدِ وَكَانَ فِي قَصْرِ الْمَلِكِ شَبَابِيكُ تُطِلُّ عَلَى بُسْتَانِ أَخِيهِ فَنَظَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-sāfara akhūhu waḥdahu ilā al-ṣaydi wa-kāna fī qaṣri al-maliki shabābīku tuṭillu ʿalā bustāni akhīhi fa-naẓar
sentences.l: So his brother travelled by himself to the hunt. And there were in the palace of the king windows overlooking the garden of his brother, and he looked.
sentences.i: So his brother rode off alone to the hunt. Now in the king's palace there were windows that looked down upon his brother's garden; and he looked out.
sentences.n: In أَخُوةُ and وَحْدَةُ the edition writes the possessive suffix ـهُ as a tāʾ marbūṭa — read akhūhu 'his brother' and waḥdahu 'by himself'. This is a genuine Middle Arabic orthographic habit, not a printer's error, and it recurs; the ة here is the pronoun, never the feminine ending. Note too that كَانَ stays masculine singular before its plural subject شَبَابِيكُ, while the following verb تُطِلُّ takes the feminine-singular agreement normal for non-human plurals. On the referents: 'the king' here is Shahzaman in the palace given him, and 'his brother's garden' is Shahriyar's — which is why what he is about to see from the window destroys him a second time.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِبَابِ الْقَصْرِ انْفَتَحَ وَخَرَجَ مِنْهُ عِشْرُونَ جَارِيَةً وَعِشْرُونَ عَبْدًا وَامْرَأَةُ أَخِيهِ تَمْشِي بَيْنَهُمْ وَهِيَ بَدِيعَةُ الْحُسْنِ وَالْجَمَالِ حَتَّى وَصَلُوا إِلَى فِسْقِيَّةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-bābi al-qaṣri infataḥa wa-kharaja minhu ʿishrūna jāriyatan wa-ʿishrūna ʿabdan wa-imraʾatu akhīhi tamshī baynahum wa-hiya badīʿatu al-ḥusni wa-al-jamāli ḥattā waṣalū ilā fisqiyya
sentences.l: And behold, the gate of the palace — it opened, and there came out from it twenty slave-girls and twenty slaves, and the wife of his brother walking among them, she being marvellous of beauty and comeliness, until they reached a fountain-basin.
sentences.i: And lo, the palace gate was flung open, and out of it came twenty handmaidens and twenty slaves, and his brother's wife walking in their midst, marvellous in beauty and in loveliness; and they came at last to a fountain-basin.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi- ('and all at once there was…') normally governs a noun alone; here the noun bāb al-qaṣr is followed by a finite verb, infataḥa, which is a loose Middle Arabic stretching of the construction. Note also the numeral syntax: ʿishrūna takes its counted noun in the accusative singular (jāriyatan, ʿabdan), never the plural.

sentences.t: وَخَلَعُوا ثِيَابَهُمْ وَجَلَسُوا مَعَ الْعَبِيدِ وَإِذَا بِامْرَأَةِ الْمَلِكِ صَاحَتْ يَا مَسْعُودُ فَجَاءَهَا عَبْدٌ أَسْوَدُ فَعَانَقَهَا وَعَانَقَتْهُ وَوَاقَعَهَا وَكَذَلِكَ الْجَوَارِي فَعَلُوا بِهِمُ الْعَبِيدُ
sentences.tr: wa-khalaʿū thiyābahum wa-jalasū maʿa al-ʿabīdi wa-idhā bi-imraʾati al-maliki ṣāḥat yā Masʿūdu fa-jāʾahā ʿabdun aswadu fa-ʿānaqahā wa-ʿānaqathu wa-wāqaʿahā wa-kadhālika al-jawārī faʿalū bihimu al-ʿabīd
sentences.l: And they cast off their garments and sat down with the slaves, and behold, the wife of the king — she cried out, 'O Masʿūd!' and there came to her a black slave, and he embraced her and she embraced him and he lay with her; and likewise the slave-girls — the slaves did with them.
sentences.i: Then they stripped off their garments and sat down among the slaves; and lo, the king's wife cried aloud, 'Masʿūd!' whereupon a black slave came to her, and he took her in his arms and she him, and he lay with her; and even so did the slaves with the handmaidens.
sentences.n: wāqaʿa (verb III, literally 'to fall in with') is the ordinary unmarked verb for lying with a woman — the coarse vocabulary arrives only in the next unit. The closing clause is doubly non-Classical: the fronted topic al-jawārī (feminine) is resumed by a masculine pronoun, bihim, and the verb faʿalū carries its own plural ending although the subject al-ʿabīdu follows it, where Classical usage would require the singular faʿala.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا فِي بَوْسٍ وَعِنَاقٍ وَنَيْكٍ وَرِحَاقٍ حَتَّى وَلَّى النَّهَارُ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazālū fī bawsin wa-ʿināqin wa-naykin wa-riḥāqin ḥattā wallā al-nahār
sentences.l: And they did not cease in kissing and embracing and fucking and riḥāq until the day turned away.
sentences.i: Nor did they leave off kissing and embracing and fucking and [riḥāq — some further lewdness; the word is obscure] until the day had turned to its going.
sentences.n: nayk is not a clinical or polite word: it is the obscene Arabic root for sexual intercourse, the exact force of English 'fuck', and the passage is meant to be gross. The fourth item, printed ورحاق, is not attested in the dictionaries in any such sense. What is certain is that it is picked for the rhyme with عِنَاق in the sajʿ chain bawsin / ʿināqin / naykin / riḥāqin. Its meaning is a guess: siḥāq, tribadism (women with women), is the obvious candidate, though the scene described is women with men, which tells against it; the form may simply be corrupt. It is vocalized here exactly as it stands. The frame lam yazālū fī + verbal nouns ('they did not cease in…') is the normal idiom for sustained activity.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى ذَلِكَ أَخُو الْمَلِكِ قَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ بَلِيَّتِي أَخَفُّ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْبَلِيَّةِ وَقَدِ انْفَكَّ مَا عِنْدَكَ مِنَ الْغَيْرِ وَالْغَمِّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā dhālika akhū al-maliki qāla fī nafsihi wa-Allāhi inna baliyyatī akhaffu min hādhihi al-baliyyati wa-qad infakka mā ʿindaka mina al-ghayri wa-al-ghamm
sentences.l: And when the brother of the king saw that, he said within himself: By God, truly my affliction is lighter than this affliction, and there has been loosed what is with you of jealousy and grief.
sentences.i: Now when the king's brother beheld this, he said within himself: By God, my own affliction is a lighter thing than this one; and that burden of jealousy and sorrow you have borne is loosed from you.
sentences.n: The soliloquy slips into the second person: ʿindaka, 'what is with thee', is the speaker addressing himself as 'thou' — a colloquial turn kept here rather than smoothed. al-ghayr stands for ghayra, jealousy (the sense the passage requires), not ghayr 'other'; the spelling is the edition's and is preserved.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ هَذَا أَعْظَمُ مِمَّا جَرَى لِي وَلَمْ يَزَلْ فِي أَكْلٍ وَشُرْبٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla hādhā aʿẓamu mimmā jarā lī wa-lam yazal fī aklin wa-shurb
sentences.l: And he said: This is greater than what befell me — and he did not cease in eating and drinking.
sentences.i: And he said: This is a graver matter than what befell me. Thereafter he left off neither eating nor drinking.
sentences.n: The narrative reuses the frame of the previous unit — lam yazal fī + verbal nouns — but now for Shahzaman's recovered appetite, so that the couplings in the garden and his eating and drinking are cast in the same grammatical mould.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ هَذَا جَاءَ أَخُوةُ مِنَ السَّفَرِ فَسَلَّمَا عَلَى بَعْضِهِمَا وَنَظَرَ الْمَلِكُ شَهْرِيَارُ إِلَى أَخِيهِ الْمَلِكِ شَاهْزَمَانَ رَآةُ رُدَّ لَهُ لَوْنُهُ وَاحْمَرَّ وَجْهُهُ وَصَارَ يَأْكُلُ بِشَهِيَّهْ بَعْدَ مَا كَانَ قَلِيلَ الْأَكْلِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda hādhā jāʾa akhūhu mina al-safari fa-sallamā ʿalā baʿḍihimā wa-naẓara al-maliku Shahriyāru ilā akhīhi al-maliki Shāhzamāna raʾāhu rudda lahu lawnuhu wa-iḥmarra wajhuhu wa-ṣāra yaʾkulu bi-shahiyyah baʿda mā kāna qalīla al-akl
sentences.l: And after this his brother came from the journey, and the two saluted one another; and King Shahriyar looked toward his brother King Shahzaman — he saw him: his colour had been given back to him, and his face had reddened, and he had come to eat with appetite, after he had been scant of eating.
sentences.i: And thereafter his brother returned from his journeying, and the two saluted each other. King Shahriyar looked upon his brother King Shahzaman and saw that his colour was come back to him and his face grown ruddy, and that he now ate with relish, whereas before he had eaten but little.
sentences.n: The edition writes the 3ms suffix ـهُ with tāʾ marbūṭa in two places here — اخوة for akhūhu, 'his brother', and رآة for raʾāhu, 'he saw him' — and this is kept exactly as printed rather than corrected. The edition also prints ياكل without a hamza seat; the hamza is supplied here as a combining mark, so the printed letters stand unchanged and the word reads yaʾkulu. Similarly بشهيه prints a final ه where the word is normally بشهية, shahiyya; it is left as printed and read in pause. rudda is taken as a passive, 'was given back', matching qad rudda ilayka lawnuka in the next unit.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَخُوةُ الْمَلِكُ الْكَبِيرُ يَا أَخِي كُنْتُ أَرَاكَ مُصْفَرَّ اللَّوْنِ وَالْوَجْهِ وَالْآنَ قَدْ رُدَّ إِلَيْكَ لَوْنُكَ فَأَخْبِرْنِي بِحَالِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu akhūhu al-maliku al-kabīru yā akhī kuntu arāka muṣfarra al-lawni wa-al-wajhi wa-al-āna qad rudda ilayka lawnuka fa-akhbirnī bi-ḥālik
sentences.l: So his brother, the elder king, said to him: O my brother, I used to see you yellowed of colour and of face, and now your colour has been given back to you; so inform me of your state.
sentences.i: Then his brother the elder King said to him: O my brother, I used to see you wan of hue and countenance, and now your colour is come back to you; tell me, then, how it stands with you.
sentences.n: kuntu arāka, 'I was seeing you', is the ordinary way of putting a habitual or continuing state in the past. muṣfarr is the participle of the verb IX iṣfarra, 'to turn yellow' — the same verb used of Shahzaman's face when his grief first took him, so the brother's words echo the earlier description exactly. The edition prints الان without the madda; it is supplied here as a combining mark over the bare alif, so that the printed letters stand and the word still reads al-āna.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَمَّا تَغَيُّرُ لَوْنِي فَأَذْكُرُهُ لَكَ وَاعْفُ عَنِّي مِنْ إِخْبَارِي لَكَ بِرَدِّ لَوْنِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu ammā taghayyuru lawnī fa-adhkuruhu laka wa-ʿfu ʿannī min ikhbārī laka bi-raddi lawnī
sentences.l: So he said to him: As for the changing of my colour, I will relate it to you; but excuse me from my informing you of the giving-back of my colour.
sentences.i: He answered him: As for the changing of my hue, that I will recount to you; but spare me the telling of how my colour came again.
sentences.n: ammā … fa- is the standard 'as for X, then Y' frame, isolating one topic before the comment falls. The government is loose Middle Arabic: Classical usage would put the thing excused after ʿan, where the text has min ikhbārī laka, literally 'from my informing to thee', with the person told introduced by li- instead of standing as a direct object.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَخْبِرْنِي أَوَّلًا بِتَغَيُّرِ لَوْنِكَ وَضَعْفِكَ حَتَّى أَسْمَعَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu akhbirnī awwalan bi-taghayyuri lawnika wa-ḍaʿfika ḥattā asmaʿah
sentences.l: So he said to him: Inform me first of the changing of your colour and your weakness, that I may hear it.
sentences.i: He said to him: Tell me first how your colour came to change and your body came to fail; let me hear that much.
sentences.n: ḥattā here is purposive rather than temporal — with the following subjunctive asmaʿa it means 'so that I may hear', not 'until I hear'.

glossary.الْحَمْدُ: الـ + حَمْد — ḥamd, praise (m., nom.); 'the praise'
glossary.لِلَّهِ: لِـ + اللَّه — Allāh, God (gen.); 'to God, God's' (the article's alif elides after li-)
glossary.رَبِّ: rabb — lord, master (m., gen. in apposition; first term of an iḍāfa)
glossary.الْعَالَمِينَ: الـ + عَالَمِين — ʿālam, world, created realm (m. sound pl., gen.); 'the worlds'
glossary.وَالصَّلَوةُ: وَ + الـ + صَلَوة — ṣalāh, prayer, blessing (f., nom.); 'and the blessing'
glossary.وَالسَّلَامُ: وَ + الـ + سَلَام — salām, peace, greeting (m., nom.)
glossary.عَلَى: ʿalā — on, upon, over (prep.); with سَلَّمَ, 'greeted'
glossary.سَيِّدِ: sayyid — lord, chief (m., gen. after ʿalā; first term of an iḍāfa)
glossary.الْمُرْسَلِينَ: الـ + مُرْسَلِين — mursal, one sent, messenger (pass. part. of IV arsala; m. pl., gen.)
glossary.سَيِّدِنَا: سَيِّد + ـنَا — sayyid, lord (m., gen.); 'our lord'
glossary.وَمَوْلَانَا: وَ + مَوْلَى + ـنَا — mawlā, master, patron (m., gen.); 'and our master'
glossary.مُحَمَّدٍ: Muḥammad — the Prophet's name (gen. with tanwīn, in apposition to sayyid)
glossary.صَلَّى: ṣallā — to bless, invoke blessing upon (verb II, perf. 3ms; with ʿalā)
glossary.اللَّهُ: Allāh — God (nom.; the name is treated as a single indivisible word)
glossary.عَلَيْهِ: عَلَى + ـهِ — ʿalā, on, upon (prep.) + 3ms; 'upon him'
glossary.وَسَلَّمَ: وَ + سَلَّمَ — sallama, to greet, salute, grant peace (verb II, perf. 3ms); with عَلَى
glossary.صَلَوةً: صَلَوة — ṣalāh, blessing (f., acc. as cognate object of ṣallā)
glossary.وَسَلَامًا: وَ + سَلَام — salām, peace (m., acc. as cognate object of sallama)
glossary.دَائِمَيْنِ: دَائِم (dual) — dāʾim, lasting, perpetual (act. part. of dāma; m. dual acc.)
glossary.مُتَلَازِمَيْنِ: مُتَلَازِم (dual) — mutalāzim, mutually inseparable, each attending the other (act. part. of VI talāzama; m. dual acc.)
glossary.إِلَى: ilā — to, toward, up to (prep.); with أَنْ + perfect, 'until'
glossary.يَوْمِ: yawm — day (m., gen. after ilā; first term of an iḍāfa)
glossary.الدِّينِ: الـ + دِين — dīn, judgment, requital, religion (m., gen.); yawm al-dīn = the Day of Judgment
glossary.وَبَعْدُ: وَ + بَعْدُ — baʿd, after (adv., indeclinable in -u); the formula 'and now, to proceed'
glossary.فَإِنَّ: فَـ + إِنَّ — fa-, so/then + inna, indeed, verily (particle putting its subject in the acc.)
glossary.سِيَرَ: سِيَر — sīra, life-story, career, biography (f. pl. of sīra; acc. as subject of inna)
glossary.الْأَوَّلِينَ: الـ + أَوَّلِين — awwal, first, former (m. pl., gen.); 'those of old, the ancients'
glossary.صَارَتْ: ṣāra — to become (verb I hollow, perf. 3fs; takes an acc. predicate)
glossary.عِبْرَةً: عِبْرَة — ʿibra, admonition, object-lesson, warning example (f., acc.)
glossary.لِلْآخِرِينَ: لِـ + الـ + آخِرِين — ākhir, latter, one who comes after (m. pl., gen.); 'for those who come after'
glossary.لِيَرَى: لِـ + يَرَى — raʾā, to see (verb I, imperf. 3ms subjunctive after the lām of purpose)
glossary.الْإِنْسَانُ: الـ + إِنْسَان — insān, human being, man (m., nom. as subject)
glossary.الْعِبَرَ: الـ + عِبَر — ʿibra, lesson (f. pl. ʿibar; acc. as object of yarā)
glossary.الَّتِي: allatī — who, which (rel. pron., f. sg.; the form used with non-human plurals as well)
glossary.حَصَلَتْ: ḥaṣala — to occur, come about, befall (verb I, perf. 3fs)
glossary.لِغَيْرِهِ: لِـ + غَيْر + ـهِ — ghayr, other-than (m., gen.); 'to someone other than himself'
glossary.فَيَعْتَبِرَ: فَـ + يَعْتَبِر — iʿtabara, to take warning, draw a lesson (verb VIII, imperf. 3ms subjunctive, coordinated with li-yarā)
glossary.وَيُطَالِعَ: وَ + يُطَالِع — ṭālaʿa, to peruse, look into, study (verb III, imperf. 3ms subjunctive)
glossary.حَدِيثَ: ḥadīth — account, narrative, report (m., acc. as object)
glossary.الْأُمَمِ: الـ + أُمَم — umma, nation, community (f. pl. umam; gen.)
glossary.السَّالِفَةِ: الـ + سَالِفَة — sālif, past, bygone (act. part.; f. sg. agreeing with the non-human pl., gen.)
glossary.وَمَا: وَ + مَا — mā, that which, what (rel. pron.)
glossary.جَرَى: jarā — to run, happen, come to pass, befall (verb I final-weak, perf. 3ms)
glossary.لَهُمْ: لِـ + ـهُمْ — li-, to + 3mp suffix; 'to them' (li- takes fatḥa before a suffix)
glossary.فَيَنْزَجِرَ: فَـ + يَنْزَجِر — inzajara, to be restrained, deterred, pull back (verb VII, imperf. 3ms subjunctive)
glossary.فَسُبْحَانَ: فَـ + سُبْحَان — subḥān, glorification (m., acc. in the fixed formula 'glory be to')
glossary.مَنْ: man — he who, the one who (rel. pron.)
glossary.جَعَلَ: jaʿala — to make, render, appoint (verb I, perf. 3ms; takes two objects)
glossary.لِقَوْمِ: لِـ + قَوْم — qawm, people, folk (m., gen.); 'for the folk of'
glossary.الْآخِرِينَ: الـ + آخِرِين — ākhir, latter, one who comes after (m. pl., gen.)
glossary.فَمِنْ: فَـ + مِنْ — min, from, of, among (prep.)
glossary.ذَلِكَ: dhālika — that (dem. pron., m. sg., invariable in form); فَمِنْ ذَلِكَ = 'an instance of that is'
glossary.الْعِبَرُ: الـ + عِبَر — ʿibra, admonition, object-lesson (f. pl. ʿibar; nom. as subject)
glossary.الْحِكَايَاتُ: الـ + حِكَايَات — ḥikāya, tale, story (f. pl.; nom., in apposition to al-ʿibar)
glossary.تُسَمَّى: sammā — to name, call (verb II); passive imperf. 3fs tusammā, 'is called'
glossary.أَلْفَ: alf — thousand (m., acc. as the retained second object of the passive)
glossary.لَيْلَةٍ: لَيْلَة — layla, night (f., gen. sg. as the counted noun after alf)
glossary.وَلَيْلَةً: وَ + لَيْلَة — layla, night (f., acc., coordinated with alfa)
glossary.فِيهَا: فِي + ـهَا — fī, in + 3fs suffix; 'in them' (referring to the f. pl. tales)
glossary.مِنَ: min — from, of, among, than (prep.; the nūn takes the linking vowel -a before the article)
glossary.السِّيَرِ: الـ + سِيَر — sīra, life-story, career (f. pl. siyar; gen.)
glossary.الْجَلِيلَةِ: الـ + جَلِيلَة — jalīl, noble, majestic, weighty (adj., f. sg. agreeing with a non-human pl., gen.)
glossary.وَالْأَمْثَالِ: وَ + الـ + أَمْثَال — mathal, proverb, exemplary saying (m. pl. amthāl; gen.)
glossary.فَقَدْ: فَـ + قَدْ — qad, indeed, already (particle before a perfect verb)
glossary.حُكِيَ: ḥakā — to relate, recount (verb I defective); passive perf. 3ms ḥukiya, 'it was related'
glossary.وَاللَّهُ: وَ + اللَّه — Allāh, God (nom., subject of a parenthetical circumstantial clause)
glossary.أَعْلَمُ: aʿlam — more/most knowing (elative of ʿalima; m., nom. as predicate)
glossary.بِغَيْبِهِ: بِـ + غَيْب + ـهِ — ghayb, the hidden, the unseen (m., gen.); 'of His unseen'
glossary.وَأَحْكَمُ: وَ + أَحْكَم — aḥkam, wiser (elative of ḥakīm)
glossary.وَأَعَزُّ: وَ + أَعَزّ — aʿazz, mightier, more exalted (elative of ʿazīz)
glossary.وَأَكْرَمُ: وَ + أَكْرَم — akram, more generous, more noble (elative of karīm)
glossary.وَأَلْطَفُ: وَ + أَلْطَف — alṭaf, more gracious, more subtly kind (elative of laṭīf)
glossary.وَأَرْحَمُ: وَ + أَرْحَم — arḥam, more merciful (elative of raḥīm)
glossary.فِيمَا: فِي + مَا — fī, in, concerning + mā, that which; 'concerning what'
glossary.مَضَى: maḍā — to pass, elapse, go by (verb I defective, perf. 3ms)
glossary.وَتَقَدَّمَ: وَ + تَقَدَّمَ — taqaddama, to go before, precede (verb V, perf. 3ms)
glossary.وَنُسْلِفُ: وَ + نُسْلِف — aslafa, to send ahead, set forth in advance (verb IV, imperf. 1pl indic.); anomalous here (see note)
glossary.مِنْ: min — from, of, among, than (prep.); also explicative, 'consisting of'
glossary.أَحَادِيثِ: أَحَادِيث — ḥadīth, account, report (m. pl. aḥādīth; gen.)
glossary.أَنَّهُ: أَنَّ + ـهُ — anna, that (subordinating particle) + 3ms pronoun as its grammatical subject; 'that (it was so)'
glossary.كَانَ: kāna — to be, to happen; existential 'there was' (verb I hollow, perf. 3ms); with a following verb it frames the tense
glossary.فِي: fī — in, within, among, at (prep.); before a verbal noun, 'engaged in'
glossary.قَدِيمِ: qadīm — old, ancient (adj. used as a noun, m., gen.); qadīm al-zamān = 'olden time'
glossary.الزَّمَانِ: الـ + زَمَان — zamān, time, age (m., gen.)
glossary.وَسَالِفِ: وَ + سَالِف — sālif, that which is past, bygone (act. part. of salafa; m., gen.)
glossary.الْعَصْرِ: الـ + عَصْر — ʿaṣr, era, epoch (m., gen.)
glossary.وَالْأَوَانِ: وَ + الـ + أَوَان — awān, time, season, period (m., gen.)
glossary.مَلِكٌ: malik — king (m., nom. indef.; the delayed subject of kāna)
glossary.مُلُوكِ: مُلُوك — malik, king (m. pl. mulūk; gen.)
glossary.بَنِي: بَنِي — banū, sons of, tribe of (m. pl. of ibn; gen. banī in construct)
glossary.سَاسَانَ: Sāsān — Sasan, eponym of the Sasanian kings (proper name, diptote: gen. in -a without tanwīn)
glossary.بِجَزَائِرِ: بِـ + جَزَائِر — jazīra, island (f. pl. jazāʾir; gen.); bi- here locative, 'in the isles of'
glossary.صَاحِبُ: ṣāḥib — companion, possessor, master of (m., nom., in apposition to malikun)
glossary.وَأَعْوَانٍ: وَ + أَعْوَان — ʿawn, helper, auxiliary (m. pl. aʿwān; gen. indef.)
glossary.وَخَدَمٍ: وَ + خَدَم — khādim, servant (collective pl. khadam; gen. indef.)
glossary.وَحَشَمٍ: وَ + حَشَم — ḥasham, retinue, household attendants, entourage (coll.; gen. indef.)
glossary.وَكَانَ: وَ + كَانَ — kāna, to be (verb I hollow, perf. 3ms); often existential, 'there was/were', and with لِـ + suffix, 'he had'
glossary.لَهُ: لِـ + ـهُ — li-, to, for, belonging to (prep.) + 3ms suffix; 'to him, for him'
glossary.وَلَدَانِ: وَلَد (dual) — walad, son, child (m. dual nom.); subject of kāna
glossary.أَحَدُهُمَا: أَحَد + ـهُمَا — aḥad, one (m., nom.) + 3m dual suffix; 'one of the two'
glossary.كَبِيرٌ: kabīr — big, great; here 'elder' (adj., m. nom. indef.)
glossary.وَالْآخَرُ: وَ + الـ + آخَر — ākhar, the other (m., nom.)
glossary.صَغِيرٌ: ṣaghīr — small, little; here 'younger' (adj., m. nom. indef.)
glossary.وَكَانَا: وَ + كَانَ + ـا — kāna, to be (perf. 3m dual); 'and the two were'
glossary.فَارِسَيْنِ: فَارِس (dual) — fāris, horseman, knight (m. dual acc. as predicate of kānā)
glossary.بَطَلَيْنِ: بَطَل (dual) — baṭal, champion, hero (m. dual acc.)
glossary.الْأَكْبَرُ: الـ + أَكْبَر — akbar, greater, elder (elative of kabīr; m., nom.)
glossary.أَفْرَسَ: afras — more skilled as a horseman (elative formed from the noun fāris; m., acc. as predicate of kāna; diptote)
glossary.الْأَصْغَرِ: الـ + أَصْغَر — aṣghar, smaller, younger (elative of ṣaghīr; m., gen.)
glossary.وَقَدْ: وَ + قَدْ — qad, indeed, already (with a perfect verb it gives pluperfect force)
glossary.مَلَكَ: malaka — to own, hold, rule over (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.الْبِلَادَ: الـ + بِلَاد — balad, land, town, territory (m. pl. bilād; acc. as object)
glossary.وَحَكَمَ: وَ + حَكَمَ — ḥakama, to judge, govern, pass sentence (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.بِالْعَدْلِ: بِـ + الـ + عَدْل — ʿadl, justice, equity (m., gen.); 'with justice'
glossary.الرَّعِيَّةِ: الـ + رَعِيَّة — raʿiyya, the subjects, the flock ruled over (f. coll., gen.)
glossary.وَأَحَبُّوهُ: وَ + أَحَبُّوا + ـهُ — aḥabba, to love (verb IV doubled, perf. 3mp) + 3ms object suffix; 'and they loved him'
glossary.أَهْلُ: ahl — people, folk, inhabitants (m., nom.; the subject following the verb)
glossary.بِلَادِهِ: بِلَاد + ـهِ — balad, land, town (m.; broken pl. بِلَاد, taking f. sg. agreement as non-human plurals do; gen.) + 3ms poss.; 'his lands'
glossary.وَمَمْلَكَتِهِ: وَ + مَمْلَكَة + ـهِ — mamlaka, kingdom, realm (f., gen.); 'and his kingdom'
glossary.اسْمُهُ: اسْم + ـهُ — ism, name (m., nom.); 'his name' (the initial alif is hamzat al-waṣl and is elided in reading)
glossary.الْمَلِكَ: الـ + مَلِك — malik, king (m., acc. as predicate of kāna)
glossary.شَهْرِيَارَ: Shahriyār — Persian name, roughly 'lord of the realm' (proper name, diptote: acc. in -a without tanwīn)
glossary.أَخُوهُ: أَخ + ـهُ — akh, brother (m.; one of the 'five nouns', nom. form أَخُو) + 3ms poss.; 'his brother'
glossary.الصَّغِيرُ: الـ + صَغِير — ṣaghīr, small; here 'younger' (adj., m., nom.)
glossary.شَاهْ: shāh — king (Persian loanword); indeclinable first element of the name Shāh Zamān, the case falling on زَمَان
glossary.زَمَانَ: zamān — time, age (m.); second element of Shāh Zamān, 'king of the age' (acc., diptote as part of a foreign proper name)
glossary.مَلِكَ: malik — king (m., acc. as predicate of kāna; first term of an iḍāfa)
glossary.سَمَرْقَنْدَ: Samarqand — the city in Transoxiana (proper name, diptote: gen. in -a)
glossary.الْعَجَمِ: الـ + عَجَم — ʿajam, the non-Arabs, esp. the Persians (coll., gen.)
glossary.وَلَمْ: وَ + لَمْ — wa-, and (conj.) + lam, not (negative particle governing the jussive and negating the past)
glossary.يَزَالَا: zāla — to cease (verb I, imperf. jussive 3rd dual, nūn dropped); with lam: 'the two did not cease'
glossary.مُسْتَمِرَّيْنِ: mustamirr — continuing, going on (act. part. of istamarra, verb X; dual acc./gen., predicate of lam yazālā)
glossary.بِلَادِهِمَا: بِلَاد + ـهِمَا — bilād, lands, country (f. pl. of balad) + 3rd dual poss. suffix; 'their two lands'
glossary.وَكُلُّ: وَ + كُلُّ — wa, and (here circumstantial 'with, while') + kull, each, every (m., nom. as subject of a nominal clause)
glossary.وَاحِدٍ: wāḥid — one (numeral/noun, m. gen. as second term of the iḍāfa); 'each one'
glossary.مَمْلَكَتِهِ: مَمْلَكَة + ـهِ — mamlaka, kingdom, realm (f.) + 3ms poss.; 'his kingdom'
glossary.حَاكِمٌ: ḥākim — ruler, governor, one who judges (act. part. of ḥakama, verb I; m. nom. as predicate)
glossary.عَادِلٌ: ʿādil — just, equitable (act. part. of ʿadala; m. nom., adjective agreeing with ḥākim)
glossary.رَعِيَّتِهِ: رَعِيَّة + ـهِ — raʿiyya, flock, subjects of a ruler (f.) + 3ms poss.; 'his subjects'
glossary.مُدَّةَ: mudda — period, span of time (f., acc. as adverb of duration, first term of iḍāfa)
glossary.عِشْرِينَ: ʿishrūn — twenty (numeral, oblique form in ـينَ)
glossary.سَنَةً: sana — year (f., acc. sing. as the counted noun after 11–99)
glossary.غَايَةِ: ghāya — utmost degree, extreme (f., gen. after fī); fī ghāyati X = 'in the utmost of X'
glossary.الْبَسْطِ: الـ + بَسْط — basṭ, expansiveness, cheer, good spirits (m., gen.)
glossary.وَالِانْشِرَاحِ: وَ + الـ + انْشِرَاح — inshirāḥ, gladness, lightness of heart (verbal noun of insharaḥa, verb VII; m., gen.)
glossary.الْحَالَةِ: الـ + حَالَة — ḥāla, state, condition (f., gen. after عَلَى)
glossary.فَعِنْدَ: فَـ + عِنْدَ — fa, so, and then (conj.) + ʿinda, at, by (adverbial prep.); ʿinda dhālika = 'at that point'
glossary.اشْتَاقَ: ishtāqa — to long for, yearn (verb VIII of shawq, perf. 3ms); construed with ilā
glossary.الْمَلِكُ: الـ + مَلِك — malik, king (m., nom. sg., as subject or in apposition)
glossary.الْكَبِيرُ: الـ + كَبِير — kabīr, great, elder (adj., m. nom. sg.); 'the elder'
glossary.أَخِيهِ: أَخ + ـهِ — akh, brother (m.; one of the 'five nouns', oblique form أَخِي) + 3ms poss.; 'his brother'
glossary.الصَّغِيرِ: الـ + صَغِير — ṣaghīr, small, younger (adj., m. gen., agreeing with akhīhi)
glossary.فَأَمَرَ: فَـ + أَمَرَ — fa, so (conj.) + amara, to command, order (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.وَزِيرَهُ: وَزِير + ـهُ — wazīr, vizier, chief minister (m., acc. as object) + 3ms poss.
glossary.أَنْ: an — that (subordinating particle governing the subjunctive); after إِلَى it forms 'until'
glossary.يُسَافِرَ: sāfara — to travel, set out on a journey (verb III, imperf. subjunctive 3ms after an)
glossary.عِنْدِ: ʿinda — at, with, in the presence of (adverbial prep.; gen. عِنْدِ here because إِلَى governs it, as in مِنْ عِنْدِهِ)
glossary.وَيُحْضِرَ: وَ + يُحْضِرَ — wa, and + aḥḍara, to bring, cause to be present (verb IV, imperf. subjunctive 3ms, still under an)
glossary.بِهِ: بِـ + ـهِ — bi-, with, by, in (prep.) + 3ms suffix; often simply marks the object, 'him'
glossary.فَأَجَابَهُ: فَـ + أَجَابَ + ـهُ — ajāba, to answer, reply (verb IV, perf. 3ms) + 3ms obj.; 'so he answered him'
glossary.بِالسَّمْعِ: بِـ + الـ + سَمْع — samʿ, hearing, hearkening (m., gen. after بِـ); first half of the obedience formula
glossary.وَالطَّاعَةِ: وَ + الـ + طَاعَة — ṭāʿa, obedience (f., gen.); second half of the obedience formula
glossary.وَسَافَرَ: وَ + سَافَرَ — sāfara, to travel (verb III, perf. 3ms)
glossary.وَصَلَ: waṣala — to arrive, reach (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.بِالسَّلَامَةِ: بِـ + الـ + سَلَامَة — salāma, safety, soundness (f., gen.); bi-l-salāma = 'safely'
glossary.وَدَخَلَ: وَ + دَخَلَ — dakhala, to enter, go in (verb I, perf. 3ms); takes its goal directly or with a preposition
glossary.وَبَلَّغَهُ: وَ + بَلَّغَ + ـهُ — ballagha, to convey, deliver (verb II, perf. 3ms) + 3ms indir. obj.; 'and he delivered to him'
glossary.السَّلَامَ: الـ + سَلَام — salām, greeting, salutation of peace (m., acc. as object)
glossary.وَأَعْلَمَهُ: وَ + أَعْلَمَ + ـهُ — aʿlama, to inform, let know (verb IV, perf. 3ms) + 3ms obj.
glossary.أَنَّ: anna — that (particle introducing a nominal clause; its subject takes the accusative)
glossary.أَخَاهُ: أَخ + ـهُ — akh, brother (m., acc. 'five nouns' form akhā-) + 3ms poss.; subject of anna
glossary.مُشْتَاقٌ: mushtāq — longing, yearning (act. part. of ishtāqa, verb VIII; m. nom. as predicate of anna)
glossary.إِلَيْهِ: إِلَى + ـهِ — ilā, to, toward (prep., pre-suffix form ilay-) + 3ms; 'to him, for him'
glossary.وَقَصْدَهُ: وَ + قَصْد + ـهُ — qaṣd, aim, intent, purpose (m., acc. as a second subject of anna) + 3ms poss.
glossary.بِزِيَارَتِهِ: بِـ + زِيَارَة + ـهِ — ziyāra, visit, visiting (f., verbal noun of zāra; gen. after bi) + 3ms obj. poss.; 'in visiting him'
glossary.وَتَجَهَّزَ: وَ + تَجَهَّزَ — tajahhaza, to equip oneself, make ready (verb V, perf. 3ms)
glossary.لِلسَّفَرِ: لِـ + الـ + سَفَر — safar, travel, journey (m., gen. after li); 'for the journey'
glossary.وَأَخْرَجَ: وَ + أَخْرَجَ — akhraja, to bring out, send forth (verb IV, perf. 3ms)
glossary.خِيَامَهُ: خِيَام + ـهُ — khiyām, tents (f. pl. of khayma; acc. as object) + 3ms poss.
glossary.وَجِمَالَهُ: وَ + جِمَال + ـهُ — jimāl, camels (pl. of jamal; acc.) + 3ms poss.
glossary.وَبِغَالَهُ: وَ + بِغَال + ـهُ — bighāl, mules (pl. of baghl; acc.) + 3ms poss.
glossary.وَخَدَمَهُ: وَ + خَدَم + ـهُ — khadam, servants, attendants (collective; acc.) + 3ms poss.
glossary.وَأَعْوَانَهُ: وَ + أَعْوَان + ـهُ — aʿwān, helpers, aides, retainers (pl. of ʿawn; acc.) + 3ms poss.
glossary.وَأَقَامَ: وَ + أَقَامَ — aqāma, to set up, appoint, install (verb IV, perf. 3ms)
glossary.حَاكِمًا: ḥākim — ruler, governor (act. part. of ḥakama; m. acc. as ḥāl / second object); 'as ruler'
glossary.وَخَرَجَ: وَ + خَرَجَ — kharaja, to go out, come forth, depart (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.طَالِبًا: ṭālib — seeking, making for (act. part. of ṭalaba; m. acc. as ḥāl); 'seeking, bound for'
glossary.بِلَادَ: bilād — lands, country (f. pl.; acc. as object of ṭāliban, first term of iḍāfa)
glossary.فَلَمَّا: فَـ + لَمَّا — fa-, and so (conj.) + lammā, when, as soon as (temporal particle taking the perfect)
glossary.نِصْفِ: niṣf — half, middle (m., gen. after fī, first term of iḍāfa)
glossary.اللَّيْلِ: الـ + لَيْل — layl, night (m., gen.); niṣf al-layl = 'midnight'
glossary.تَذَكَّرَ: tadhakkara — to remember, call to mind (verb V, perf. 3ms)
glossary.حَاجَةً: ḥāja — need, thing needed, errand (f., acc. indef. as object)
glossary.نَسِيَهَا: نَسِيَ + ـهَا — nasiya, to forget (verb I, perf. 3ms) + 3fs obj.; 'which he had forgotten'
glossary.قَصْرِهِ: قَصْر + ـهِ — qaṣr, palace, castle (m., gen.) + 3ms poss.
glossary.فَرَجَعَ: فَـ + رَجَعَ — rajaʿa, to return, go back (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.قَصْرَهُ: قَصْر + ـهُ — qaṣr, palace (m., acc. as object of dakhala) + 3ms poss.
glossary.فَوَجَدَ: فَـ + وَجَدَ — wajada, to find (verb I, perf. 3ms); takes an object plus an accusative complement
glossary.زَوْجَتَهُ: زَوْجَة + ـهُ — zawja, wife (f., acc. as object) + 3ms poss.
glossary.رَاقِدَةً: rāqida — lying down, asleep (act. part. of raqada; f. acc. as ḥāl)
glossary.فِرَاشِهِ: فِرَاش + ـهِ — firāsh, bed, bedding (m., gen.) + 3ms poss.
glossary.مُعَانِقَةً: muʿāniqa — embracing, holding in the arms (act. part. of ʿānaqa, verb III; f. acc. as second ḥāl)
glossary.عَبْدًا: ʿabd — slave (m., acc. indef.); object of a participle, or tamyīz after a numeral
glossary.أَسْوَدَ: aswad — black (adj. of the af ʿal colour pattern; diptote, so acc. without tanwīn)
glossary.بَعْضِ: baʿḍ — some, a part of, one of (m., gen.; first term of a construct); مِنْ بَعْضِ = 'one of'
glossary.الْعَبِيدِ: الـ + عَبِيد — ʿabd (broken pl. عَبِيد), slave (m., gen. pl.); 'the slaves'
glossary.رَأَى: raʾā — to see, behold (verb I, perf. 3ms, final-weak)
glossary.هَذَا: hādhā — this (dem. pron., m. sg., invariable in form)
glossary.الْأَمْرَ: الـ + أَمْر — amr, matter, affair, thing (m., acc. as object of raʾā)
glossary.اسْوَدَّتِ: iswadda — to turn black, blacken (verb IX, the colour form, perf. 3fs); final kasra is liaison before the article
glossary.الدُّنْيَا: الـ + دُنْيَا — dunyā, the world, this lower world (f., nom. as subject; indeclinable in ā)
glossary.وَجْهِهِ: وَجْه + ـهِ — wajh, face (m., gen. after fī) + 3ms poss.; 'his face'
glossary.وَقَالَ: وَ + قَالَ — qāla, to say (verb I hollow, perf. 3ms); 'and he said'
glossary.نَفْسِهِ: نَفْس + ـهِ — nafs, self, soul (f., gen.) + 3ms poss.; فِي نَفْسِهِ = 'within himself, inwardly'
glossary.الْأَمْرُ: الـ + أَمْر — amr, matter, affair (m., nom. as subject of kāna)
glossary.قَدْ: qad — particle before the perfect marking completion; 'already, indeed'
glossary.وَقَعَ: waqaʿa — to fall, occur, come to pass (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.وَأَنَا: وَ + أَنَا — wa, here circumstantial 'while' + anā, I (1st sing. independent pronoun)
glossary.مَا: mā — (1) what, that which (rel. pron.); (2) not (negative particle before a perfect verb, a Middle Arabic usage where Classical prose has lam)
glossary.فَارَقْتُ: fāraqa — to part from, leave (verb III, perf. 1st sing.); 'I have left'
glossary.الْمَدِينَةَ: الـ + مَدِينَة — madīna, city (f., acc. as object)
glossary.فَكَيْفَ: فَـ + كَيْفَ — fa, then (apodosis marker) + kayfa, how (interrogative)
glossary.حَالُ: ḥāl — state, condition, case (m./f., nom. as subject, first term of iḍāfa)
glossary.الْمَلْعُونَةِ: الـ + مَلْعُونَة — malʿūna, accursed woman, damned one (pass. part. of laʿana; f., gen.)
glossary.لَمَّا: lammā — when (temporal particle; here with the imperfect for future time)
glossary.أَغِيبُ: ghāba — to be absent, be away (verb I, imperf. 1st sing., hollow); 'I am away'
glossary.عِنْدَ: ʿinda — at, with, in the presence of (adverbial prep.; acc. عِنْدَ, gen. عِنْدِ when another preposition governs it)
glossary.أَخِي: أَخ + ـي — akh, brother (m.; 'five nouns' form) + 1st sg. poss.; 'my brother', here vocative
glossary.مُدَّةً: mudda — a period, a space of time (f., acc. indef. as adverb of duration)
glossary.إِنَّهُ: إِنَّ + ـهُ — inna, indeed, verily (particle taking an accusative subject) + 3ms suffix, here a dummy pronoun; ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ is simply a narrative 'then'
glossary.سَحَبَ: saḥaba — to draw, drag, pull out (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.سَيْفَهُ: سَيْف + ـهُ — sayf, sword (m., acc. as object) + 3ms poss.
glossary.وَضَرَبَ: وَ + ضَرَبَ — ḍaraba, to strike, smite (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.الِاثْنَيْنِ: الـ + اثْنَيْنِ — ithnān, two, the pair (numeral; oblique/acc. dual form with hamzat waṣl); 'the two of them'
glossary.وَقَتَلَهُمَا: وَ + قَتَلَ + ـهُمَا — qatala, to kill, slay (verb I, perf. 3ms) + 3rd dual obj.; 'and he killed them both'
glossary.الْفِرَاشِ: الـ + فِرَاش — firāsh, bed, bedding (m., gen. after fī)
glossary.وَرَجَعَ: وَ + رَجَعَ — rajaʿa, to return, go back (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.وَقْتِهِ: وَقْت + ـهِ — waqt, time, moment (m., gen.) + 3ms poss.
glossary.وَسَاعَتِهِ: وَ + سَاعَة + ـهِ — sāʿa, hour, instant (f., gen.) + 3ms poss.; the doublet means 'that same instant'
glossary.وَأَمَرَ: وَ + أَمَرَ — amara, to command, order (verb I, perf. 3ms); with bi, 'to give orders for'
glossary.بِالرَّحِيلِ: بِـ + الـ + رَحِيل — raḥīl, departure, breaking camp, setting out (m., gen. after bi)
glossary.وَسَارَ: وَ + سَارَ — sāra, to travel, journey, set off (verb I, perf. 3ms); wa-, and
glossary.مَدِينَةِ: madīna — city (f.); genitive as first term of a construct
glossary.قَرُبَ: qaruba — to be near, draw near (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.مَدِينَتَهُ: مَدِينَة + ـهُ — madīna, city (f.), accusative; 'his city'
glossary.الْمُبَشِّرِينَ: الـ + مُبَشِّرِين — mubashshir, bringer of good news, herald (act. part. II of بشّر); sound m. pl., accusative
glossary.بِقُدُومِهِ: بِـ + قُدُوم + ـهِ — qudūm, arrival, coming (m., verbal noun); 'with (the news of) his arrival'
glossary.فَخَرَجَ: فَـ + خَرَجَ — kharaja, to go out, come forth (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.وَلَاقَاهُ: وَ + لَاقَى + ـهُ — lāqā, to meet, encounter (verb III, perf. 3ms); 'and he met him'
glossary.وَفَرِحَ: وَ + فَرِحَ — fariḥa, to rejoice, be glad (verb I, perf. 3ms); with بِـ at what
glossary.غَايَةَ: ghāya — utmost degree, extreme (f.); adverbial accusative, first term of a construct
glossary.الْفَرَحِ: الـ + فَرَح — faraḥ, joy, gladness (m., verbal noun); genitive
glossary.وَزَيَّنَ: وَ + زَيَّنَ — zayyana, to adorn, decorate (verb II, perf. 3ms)
glossary.وَجَلَسَ: وَ + جَلَسَ — jalasa, to sit, sit down (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.مَعَهُ: مَعَ + ـهُ — maʿa, with (prep. of accompaniment); 'with him'
glossary.يَتَحَدَّثُ: yataḥaddathu — to talk, converse (verb V, impf. 3ms); circumstantial
glossary.وَيَنْشَرِحُ: وَ + يَنْشَرِحُ — insharaḥa, to be expanded, be gladdened, take delight (verb VII, impf. 3ms); lit. 'his breast is opened'
glossary.فَتَذَكَّرَ: فَـ + تَذَكَّرَ — tadhakkara, to remember, call to mind (verb V, perf. 3ms)
glossary.زَمَانُ: zamān — time, age (m.); second element of Shāh Zamān, 'king of the age' (nom. as subject; diptote, so -u without tanwīn)
glossary.أَمْرِ: amr — affair, matter, business (m.); genitive after مِنْ
glossary.فَحَصَلَ: فَـ + حَصَلَ — ḥaṣala, to come about, occur, befall (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.عِنْدَهُ: عِنْدَ + ـهُ — ʿinda, at, with, in the possession of (prep.); 'with him', i.e. he felt it
glossary.غَمٌّ: ghamm — grief, distress, gloom (m.); nominative indefinite subject
glossary.زَايِدٌ: zāyid (Class. zāʾid) — increasing, excessive (act. part. I of زاد); adjective agreeing with غَمّ
glossary.وَاصْفَرَّ: وَ + اصْفَرَّ — iṣfarra, to turn yellow, grow sallow (verb IX, perf. 3ms)
glossary.لَوْنُهُ: لَوْن + ـهُ — lawn, colour, complexion (m., nom. sg.) + 3ms suffix; 'his colour'
glossary.وَضَعُفَ: وَ + ضَعُفَ — ḍaʿufa, to become weak (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.جِسْمُهُ: جِسْم + ـهُ — jism, body (m.); 'his body', nominative subject
glossary.رَآهُ: رَأَى + ـهُ — raʾā, to see (verb I, perf. 3ms, defective); 'he saw him'
glossary.ظَنَّ: ẓanna — to think, suppose, surmise (verb I, perf. 3ms, doubled)
glossary.بِسَبَبِ: بِـ + سَبَب — sabab, cause, reason (m.); 'by reason of, because of'
glossary.مُفَارَقَتِهِ: مُفَارَقَة + ـهِ — mufāraqa, parting-from, separation (f., verbal noun III); 'his parting from'
glossary.بِلَادَهُ: بِلَاد + ـهُ — bilād, lands, country (f. pl. of بَلَد); accusative object of the verbal noun; 'his lands'
glossary.وَمُلْكَهُ: وَ + مُلْك + ـهُ — mulk, kingship, dominion, realm (m.); accusative; 'and his kingdom'
glossary.فَتَرَكَ: فَـ + تَرَكَ — taraka, to leave, let be, abandon (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.سَبِيلَهُ: سَبِيل + ـهُ — sabīl, path, way (m.); accusative; in the idiom تَرَكَ سَبِيلَهُ, 'he left him to himself'
glossary.يَسْأَلْ: yasʾal — saʾala, to ask, inquire (verb I, impf. jussive 3ms after لَمْ)
glossary.الْأَيَّامِ: الـ + أَيَّام — yawm, day (m.), pl. أَيَّام; 'the days', hence 'on a certain day'
glossary.قَٰلَ: قَالَ — qāla, to say (verb I hollow, perf. 3ms); the edition prints قل without the alif, so the ā is written here with a dagger alif
glossary.إِنِّي: إِنَّ + ـي — inna, verily (particle) + 1st-person suffix; 'indeed I'
glossary.أَرَاكَ: أَرَى + ـكَ — raʾā, to see (verb I, impf. 1sg أَرَى) + 2ms object; 'I see you'
glossary.ضَعُفَ: ḍaʿufa — to become weak (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.جِسْمُكَ: جِسْم + ـكَ — jism, body (m.); 'your body' (2ms), nominative subject
glossary.لَوْنُكَ: لَوْن + ـكَ — lawn, colour, complexion (m., nom. sg.) + 2ms suffix; 'your colour'
glossary.فَقَالَ: فَـ + قَالَ — qāla, to say (verb I hollow, perf. 3ms); 'so he said'
glossary.أَنَا: anā — I (independent pron., 1sg); fronted as topic
glossary.بَاطِنِي: بَاطِن + ـي — bāṭin, inward part, interior (m., act. part. I of بطن); 'my inside'
glossary.جُرْحٌ: jurḥ — wound, gash (m.); nominative indefinite, the comment of the sentence
glossary.يُخْبِرْهُ: يُخْبِرْ + ـهُ — akhbara, to inform, tell (verb IV, impf. jussive 3ms after لَمْ) + 3ms object; 'he told him'
glossary.بِمَا: بِـ + مَا — bi-, of, about (prep.) + mā, what, that which (relative pron.)
glossary.رَأَى: raʾā — to see, behold (verb I, perf. 3ms, final-weak)
glossary.أُرِيدُ: urīdu — arāda, to want, wish (verb IV, impf. 1sg)
glossary.تُسَافِرَ: tusāfira — sāfara, to travel, set out on a journey (verb III, impf. subjunctive 2ms)
glossary.مَعِي: مَعَ + ـي — maʿa, with (prep. of accompaniment); 'with me'
glossary.الصَّيْدِ: الـ + صَيْد — ṣayd, hunting, the chase, game (m., verbal noun; gen. after إِلَى)
glossary.وَالْقَنْصِ: وَ + الـ + قَنْص — qanṣ, hunting, catching of game (m., verbal noun); near-synonym paired with صَيْد
glossary.لَعَلَّ: laʿalla — perhaps, may it be that (particle of hoping)
glossary.يَنْشَرِحَ: yanshariḥa — insharaḥa, to be expanded, be cheered (verb VII, impf. subjunctive 3ms)
glossary.خَاطِرُكَ: خَاطِر + ـكَ — khāṭir, mind, heart, spirits (m., act. part. I of خطر); 'your mind', nominative subject
glossary.فَأَبَى: فَـ + أَبَى — abā, to refuse, decline (verb I, perf. 3ms, defective)
glossary.فَسَافَرَ: فَـ + سَافَرَ — sāfara, to travel, set out (verb III, perf. 3ms)
glossary.أَخُوةُ: أَخ + ـهُ (written ة) — akh, brother (m.), nominative أَخُو + 3ms suffix; 'his brother'
glossary.وَحْدَةُ: وَحْد + ـهُ (written ة) — waḥd, aloneness (m.); adverbial accusative waḥdahu, 'by himself, alone'
glossary.قَصْرِ: qaṣr — palace, castle (m.); genitive after فِي, first term of a construct
glossary.الْمَلِكِ: الـ + مَلِك — malik, king (m., gen. sg., alone or in apposition)
glossary.شَبَابِيكُ: shubbāk, window, lattice (m.), broken pl. شَبَابِيك — diptote, so nominative without tanwīn; subject of كَانَ
glossary.تُطِلُّ: tuṭillu — aṭalla ʿalā, to look out over, overlook (verb IV, impf. 3fs, doubled); f. sg. agreeing with a non-human plural
glossary.بُسْتَانِ: bustān — garden, orchard (m., from Persian); genitive after عَلَى
glossary.فَنَظَرَ: فَـ + نَظَرَ — naẓara, to look, gaze (verb I, perf. 3ms)
glossary.وَإِذَا: وَ + إِذَا — idhā, particle of sudden discovery; 'and behold, and all at once'
glossary.بِبَابِ: بِـ + بَاب — bāb, gate, door (m., gen. sg. in construct after bi-); 'at the gate of'
glossary.الْقَصْرِ: الـ + قَصْر — qaṣr, palace, castle (m., gen. sg.); 'the palace'
glossary.انْفَتَحَ: infataḥa, to open, be opened (verb VII, perf. 3ms); 'it opened'
glossary.مِنْهُ: مِنْ + ـهُ — min, from + 3ms suffix; 'from it'
glossary.عِشْرُونَ: ʿishrūna, twenty (nom. of the sound-plural type numeral)
glossary.جَارِيَةً: jāriya, slave-girl, handmaid (f., acc. sg. as tamyīz after the numeral)
glossary.وَامْرَأَةُ: وَ + امْرَاَة — imraʾa, woman, wife (f., nom. sg. in construct; initial alif is hamzat al-waṣl, so read wa-mraʾatu); 'and the wife of'
glossary.تَمْشِي: mashā, to walk, go on foot (verb I, impf. 3fs); 'she walks, walking'
glossary.بَيْنَهُمْ: بَيْنَ + ـهُمْ — bayna, between, among + 3mp suffix; 'among them'
glossary.وَهِيَ: وَ + هِيَ — hiya, she (indep. pron. 3fs), here opening a circumstantial clause; 'she being'
glossary.بَدِيعَةُ: badīʿ (f. badīʿa), marvellous, exquisite (f. nom. sg. in construct); 'marvellous of'
glossary.الْحُسْنِ: الـ + حُسْن — ḥusn, beauty, goodliness (m., gen. sg.)
glossary.وَالْجَمَالِ: وَ + الـ + جَمَال — jamāl, beauty, comeliness (m., gen. sg.)
glossary.حَتَّى: ḥattā — until (temporal, with the perfect); so that (purposive, with the subjunctive)
glossary.وَصَلُوا: waṣala, to arrive, reach (verb I, perf. 3mp); 'they arrived'
glossary.فِسْقِيَّةٍ: fisqiyya, fountain-basin, ornamental pool (f., gen. sg. indef.)
glossary.وَخَلَعُوا: وَ + خَلَعَ — khalaʿa, to take off, cast off (verb I, perf. 3mp); 'and they cast off'
glossary.ثِيَابَهُمْ: ثِيَاب + ـهُمْ — thawb (pl. thiyāb), garment (m., acc. pl.) + 3mp suffix; 'their garments'
glossary.وَجَلَسُوا: وَ + جَلَسَ — jalasa, to sit down (verb I, perf. 3mp); 'and they sat down'
glossary.بِامْرَأَةِ: بِـ + امْرَاَة — imraʾa, woman, wife (f., gen. sg. in construct; initial alif is hamzat al-waṣl, read bi-mraʾati); 'there was the wife of'
glossary.صَاحَتْ: ṣāḥa, to cry out, shout (verb I hollow, perf. 3fs); 'she cried out'
glossary.مَسْعُودُ: Masʿūd, proper name (m., nom. as vocative; literally 'fortunate')
glossary.فَجَاءَهَا: فَـ + جَاءَ + ـهَا — jāʾa, to come (verb I, perf. 3ms) + 3fs suffix; 'so there came to her'
glossary.أَسْوَدُ: aswad, black (adj. of colour, m. nom. sg., diptote)
glossary.فَعَانَقَهَا: فَـ + عَانَقَ + ـهَا — ʿānaqa, to embrace (verb III, perf. 3ms) + 3fs obj.; 'so he embraced her'
glossary.وَعَانَقَتْهُ: وَ + عَانَقَتْ + ـهُ — ʿānaqa, to embrace (verb III, perf. 3fs) + 3ms obj.; 'and she embraced him'
glossary.وَوَاقَعَهَا: وَ + وَاقَعَ + ـهَا — wāqaʿa, to lie with, have intercourse with (verb III, perf. 3ms) + 3fs obj.; 'and he lay with her'
glossary.وَكَذَلِكَ: وَ + كَـ + ذَلِكَ — kadhālika, thus, likewise, in the same way
glossary.الْجَوَارِي: الـ + جَوَارِي — jāriya (pl. jawārī), slave-girl, handmaid (f., pl., here fronted as topic)
glossary.فَعَلُوا: faʿala, to do (verb I, perf. 3mp); 'they did'
glossary.بِهِمُ: بِـ + ـهِمْ — bi-, with + 3mp suffix (masc. used for the feminine slave-girls); 'with them'
glossary.الْعَبِيدُ: الـ + عَبِيد — ʿabd (pl. ʿabīd), slave (m., nom. pl., subject of faʿalū); 'the slaves'
glossary.يَزَالُوا: zāla (mā/lam yazal), to cease (verb I hollow, jussive 3mp); with lam: 'they did not cease'
glossary.بَوْسٍ: baws, kissing (verbal noun of bāsa, m., gen. sg. indef.)
glossary.وَعِنَاقٍ: وَ + عِنَاق — ʿināq, embracing (verbal noun of ʿānaqa, verb III, m., gen. sg. indef.)
glossary.وَنَيْكٍ: وَ + نَيْك — nayk, fucking (verbal noun of nāka, verb I; obscene register, m., gen. sg. indef.)
glossary.وَرِحَاقٍ: وَ + رِحَاق — riḥāq, obscure and probably corrupt form as printed (fiʿāl pattern like ʿināq/siḥāq); expected sense in this list is siḥāq, tribadism (gen. sg. indef.)
glossary.وَلَّى: wallā, to turn away, decline, depart (verb II, perf. 3ms); 'it turned away'
glossary.النَّهَارُ: الـ + نَهَار — nahār, day, daytime (m., nom. sg.)
glossary.أَخُو: akh, brother (m., one of the 'five nouns', nom. in -ū in construct); 'the brother of'
glossary.قَالَ: qāla, to say (verb I hollow, perf. 3ms); 'he said'
glossary.وَاللَّهِ: وَ + اللَّه — wa-Allāhi, 'by God' (the wāw of oath, wāw al-qasam, governing the genitive)
glossary.إِنَّ: inna, verily, truly (emphatic particle governing the accusative)
glossary.بَلِيَّتِي: بَلِيَّة + ـي — baliyya, affliction, calamity, trial (f., acc. after inna) + 1s suffix; 'my affliction'
glossary.أَخَفُّ: akhaff, lighter, less grievous (elative of khafīf, m. nom. sg.)
glossary.الْبَلِيَّةِ: الـ + بَلِيَّة — baliyya, affliction, calamity (f., gen. sg.)
glossary.وَقَدِ: وَ + قَدْ — qad, perfective particle 'already, indeed' (with linking vowel -i before hamzat al-waṣl)
glossary.انْفَكَّ: infakka, to be loosed, undone, released (verb VII, perf. 3ms); 'has been loosed'
glossary.عِنْدَكَ: عِنْدَ + ـكَ — ʿinda, with, in the keeping of + 2ms suffix; 'with you'
glossary.الْغَيْرِ: الـ + غَيْر — ghayr (here for ghayra), jealousy (m., gen. sg.)
glossary.وَالْغَمِّ: وَ + الـ + غَمّ — ghamm, grief, distress, gloom (m., gen. sg.)
glossary.أَعْظَمُ: aʿẓam, greater, graver (elative of ʿaẓīm, m. nom. sg.)
glossary.مِمَّا: مِنْ + مَا — min + mā, 'than that which'
glossary.لِي: لِـ + ـي — li-, to + 1s suffix; 'to me'
glossary.يَزَلْ: zāla (mā/lam yazal), to cease (verb I hollow, jussive 3ms); with lam: 'he did not cease'
glossary.أَكْلٍ: akl, eating (verbal noun of akala, m., gen. sg. indef.)
glossary.وَشُرْبٍ: وَ + شُرْب — shurb, drinking (verbal noun of shariba, m., gen. sg. indef.)
glossary.وَبَعْدَ: وَ + بَعْدَ — baʿda, after (prep. governing the genitive)
glossary.السَّفَرِ: الـ + سَفَر — safar, journey, travel (m., gen. sg.)
glossary.فَسَلَّمَا: فَـ + سَلَّمَ + ـا — sallama (ʿalā), to greet, salute (verb II, perf. 3m dual); 'so the two saluted'
glossary.بَعْضِهِمَا: بَعْض + ـهِمَا — baʿḍ, some, part (m., gen. sg.) + 3m dual suffix; idiomatically 'one another'
glossary.وَنَظَرَ: وَ + نَظَرَ — naẓara (ilā), to look (verb I, perf. 3ms); 'and he looked'
glossary.شَهْرِيَارُ: Shahriyār, proper name (m., nom.; Persian, 'lord of the realm')
glossary.شَاهْزَمَانَ: Shāhzamān, proper name (m., diptote, gen. in -a; Persian, 'king of the age')
glossary.رَآةُ: رَآ + ـةُ — raʾā, to see (verb I, perf. 3ms) + 3ms object suffix ـهُ, printed as tāʾ marbūṭa; 'he saw him'
glossary.رُدَّ: radda, to give back, restore (verb I doubled, passive perf. 3ms); 'was given back'
glossary.وَاحْمَرَّ: وَ + احْمَرَّ — iḥmarra, to turn red, grow ruddy (verb IX, perf. 3ms)
glossary.وَجْهُهُ: وَجْه + ـهُ — wajh, face (m., nom. sg.) + 3ms suffix; 'his face'
glossary.وَصَارَ: وَ + صَارَ — ṣāra, to become, come to be (verb I hollow, perf. 3ms, with following impf.); 'and he took to'
glossary.يَأْكُلُ: أَكَلَ — akala, to eat (verb I, impf. 3ms yaʾkulu); the edition prints ياكل without a hamza seat
glossary.بِشَهِيَّهْ: بِـ + شَهِيَّة — shahiyya, appetite, relish (f.; the edition prints final ه for ة); 'with appetite'
glossary.قَلِيلَ: qalīl, little, scant (adj., m. acc. sg. in construct, predicate of kāna); 'scant of'
glossary.الْأَكْلِ: الـ + اَكْل — akl, eating (verbal noun of akala, m., gen. sg.)
glossary.كُنْتُ: kāna, to be (verb I hollow, perf. 1s); with a following imperfect: 'I used to'
glossary.مُصْفَرَّ: muṣfarr, turned yellow, sallow, wan (act. part. of iṣfarra, verb IX; m. acc. sg. in construct)
glossary.اللَّوْنِ: الـ + لَوْن — lawn, colour, complexion (m., gen. sg.)
glossary.وَالْوَجْهِ: وَ + الـ + وَجْه — wajh, face, countenance (m., gen. sg.)
glossary.وَالْآنَ: وَ + الـ + اَن — al-āna, now (adverbial accusative; the edition prints alif without madda)
glossary.إِلَيْكَ: اِلَى + ـكَ — ilā, to + 2ms suffix; 'to you'
glossary.فَأَخْبِرْنِي: فَـ + اَخْبِرْ + ـنِي — akhbara, to inform, tell (verb IV, imper. 2ms) + 1s object suffix; 'so tell me'
glossary.بِحَالِكَ: بِـ + حَال + ـكَ — ḥāl, state, condition (gen. sg.) + 2ms suffix; 'of your state'
glossary.أَمَّا: ammā, as for, as to (topic particle, answered by fa-)
glossary.تَغَيُّرُ: taghayyur, change, alteration (verbal noun of taghayyara, verb V; m., nom. sg. in construct)
glossary.لَوْنِي: لَوْن + ـي — lawn, colour, complexion (m.) + 1s suffix; 'my colour'
glossary.فَأَذْكُرُهُ: فَـ + اَذْكُرُ + ـهُ — dhakara, to mention, relate (verb I, impf. 1s) + 3ms object suffix; 'then I relate it'
glossary.لَكَ: لِـ + ـكَ — li-, to + 2ms suffix; 'to you'
glossary.وَاعْفُ: وَ + اعْفُ — ʿafā (ʿafā ʿan), to pardon, excuse, let off (verb I defective, imper. 2ms); 'and excuse'
glossary.عَنِّي: عَنْ + ـي — ʿan, from, concerning + 1s suffix; 'me'
glossary.إِخْبَارِي: اِخْبَار + ـي — ikhbār, informing, telling (verbal noun of akhbara, verb IV; gen. sg.) + 1s suffix; 'my informing'
glossary.بِرَدِّ: بِـ + رَدّ — radd, giving back, restoration (verbal noun of radda; gen. sg. in construct); 'of the giving-back of'
glossary.أَخْبِرْنِي: اَخْبِرْ + ـنِي — akhbara, to inform, tell (verb IV, imper. 2ms) + 1s object suffix; 'tell me'
glossary.أَوَّلًا: awwal, first (adverbial accusative with tanwīn); 'first of all'
glossary.بِتَغَيُّرِ: بِـ + تَغَيُّر — taghayyur, change, alteration (verbal noun of taghayyara, verb V; gen. sg. in construct)
glossary.لَوْنِكَ: لَوْن + ـكَ — lawn, colour, complexion (m., gen. sg.) + 2ms suffix; 'your colour'
glossary.وَضَعْفِكَ: وَ + ضَعْف + ـكَ — ḍaʿf, weakness, feebleness (m., gen. sg.) + 2ms suffix; 'and your weakness'
glossary.أَسْمَعَهُ: اَسْمَعَ + ـهُ — samiʿa, to hear (verb I, subjunctive 1s after ḥattā) + 3ms object suffix; 'that I may hear it'
